clue.text: Yarn involving hatred

indicators.note: involving here means entangling or twisting up, so the letters of the clue word hatred are jumbled

explanation.surface: A story whose plot is driven by bitter mutual loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' reads as 'about', but here it means tangling: the letters of HATRED are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is spun fibre for knitting or sewing, the same stuff as a length of cotton.

clue.text: Water carrier in old breeches coming to Fife

parts.note: hose was the old name for close-fitting breeches or tights worn by men
a fife is a small shrill flute, a kind of pipe; the capital disguises it as the Scottish county

explanation.surface: Someone in antique trousers arriving in the Scottish county of Fife with a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a county in Scotland, but here it is the small flute played in military bands, a PIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is a flexible tube for conveying water from a tap.

clue.text: He is upset about the French opening number

indicators.note: about means going around, so the turned word wraps the rest
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word He is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A man is disturbed by the opening number of a French show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' flips the first word to EH, and 'about' wraps it round the rest; 'opening number' misleads toward a first song.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal: the position that follows tenth in a sequence is a number word.

clue.text: Store that doesn't take sides

parts.note: sounds like a neutral shop, but describes a farm building for hay that has a roof on posts and no walls

explanation.surface: A shop that stays neutral in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: This farm building is an open-sided roofed shelter where hay is stored, so it literally has no sides.

clue.text: Ordered Jonson to accept part of a wheel

indicators.note: to accept means to take inside, so the playwright's first name holds the next piece

parts.note: Ben Jonson was the Elizabethan playwright
a spoke is one of the rods joining a wheel's hub to its rim

explanation.surface: Someone told the playwright Ben Jonson to take on a wheel component.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson was an English playwright of Shakespeare's time; his first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke means made to order, as a tailored suit is.

clue.text: Bird found in Arizona

explanation.surface: Spotting a particular bird in the American Southwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical firebird reborn from its ashes; also the state capital city of Arizona, located there.

clue.text: Move a ship about before getting something to eat

indicators.note: about means around, so the ship-moving word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to kedge is to haul a ship along by a small anchor dropped ahead
ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Manoeuvre the vessel first, then get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a placing signal but supplies letters; 'about' is the container word, and 'getting' joins wordplay to definition. Kedging is a nautical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish with smoked fish and eggs, eaten at breakfast in Anglo-Indian cookery.

clue.text: Sort of pan that won't hold food?

definitions.text: Sort of pan that won't hold food?

parts.words: Sort of pan that won't hold food?
parts.note: sounds like a useless pan, but describes a coated pan to which food does not cling

explanation.surface: A pan so poor it cannot contain a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a pan has a slippery coating such as Teflon, so fried food slides off rather than clinging.

clue.text: One supporting a nomination is a mythical creature, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the creature's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a centaur is the mythical half-man, half-horse

explanation.surface: A nominee's backer turns out to be a beast of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder who formally agrees to a candidate's nomination.

clue.text: Ring with string attached

parts.note: cord is thin string or rope
on means attached, as a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A ring with a piece of string tied to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of police or troops encircling an area forms a protective ring.

clue.text: Lectures society gives away to audiences

indicators.note: to audiences means said to listeners, so a word sounding the same is used

parts.note: to peach is slang for informing on, giving someone away

explanation.surface: A society makes presentations to assembled listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACH is old slang for betraying an accomplice; spoken, 'peaches' gives the sound of the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal addresses given to a crowd, like talks by a professor.

clue.text: Creature of the nicest sort

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters of nicest are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An animal of the most pleasant kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun meaning kind, but acts as the verb 'arrange'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle or ant is a small six-legged creature.

clue.text: Loathsome person negligent about key to plant

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible, loathsome person
F is a musical key
lax means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: A despicable, careless person fumbles the key to a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' links loosely here: F stands beside LAX at its front rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild flower with yellow snapdragon-like blooms, a common hedgerow species.

clue.text: Together suddenly

explanation.surface: Things happening in unison and without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Means simultaneously, everyone at the same moment; also abruptly, without warning.

clue.text: Me and Mum knit together

parts.note: taken as written
mum means keep quiet, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A child knitting alongside their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but in 'mum's the word' it means silent: SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that engage interlock, fitting together as threads do in a net.

clue.text: Make no progress — chalk it up to me

parts.note: to chalk is to mark or write with chalk

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a rut blames themselves for the scoreboard tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers stepping on the spot without advancing: to stall, idle without moving forward.

clue.text: Coded instructions for a stew, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of for a stew could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A recipe's directions written in secret code for a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer programs are sets of instructions written in code.

clue.text: Eat very little, or a lot

explanation.surface: Someone picking at their food, or eating heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To nibble at food daintily; also a dry measure of two gallons, informally a large quantity.

clue.text: David was the second to be taken in by a fortune-teller

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the fortune-teller's word contains the letter for second

parts.note: a palmist reads fortunes from hands

explanation.surface: King David was the runner-up to be fooled by a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled; it means placed inside. David is traditionally the author of the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited as writer of the biblical hymns sung in church.

clue.text: Take tea with unaffected serviceman

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
plain means simple, unaffected

explanation.surface: Have a cup of tea with a down-to-earth soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serviceman' suggests a soldier, but this one conducts services.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a regiment or institution, who leads its religious worship.

clue.text: A cold character with fishy attributes in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: self means one's character or nature
fins are the features that mark out a fish

explanation.surface: An unfriendly personality with suspicious traits, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' reverses SELF + FINS as one run, giving SNIF + FLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor head cold with a runny nose is called by this informal name.

clue.text: Priest soaks up antiseptic

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the joined words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel
to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

explanation.surface: A clergyman absorbs a disinfectant.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is a flax-processing word meaning to soak; 'up' reverses ELI + RETS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from germs, as a surgical instrument cleaned by disinfectant is.

clue.text: Pussy has to know about one pussyfoot

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for knowing wraps the rest

parts.note: ken is the Scots verb to know
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pussyfoot is a prohibitionist, after William Pussyfoot Johnson, so a teetotaller, TT

explanation.surface: A cat must recognise someone who treads carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotal; 'pussyfoot' was a nickname for prohibitionists.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussy is a pet name for a cat, and a young one is meant here.

clue.text: Springbok — 12 run away

parts.note: 12 across is a creature with six legs, and an ant is one
elope means run away to marry

explanation.surface: A South African rugby player chased off by a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 refers to the answer INSECT; an ant is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a South African gazelle, a species of this horned grazer.

clue.text: In hospital. I composed a letter

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the clue words hospital, I composed

explanation.surface: While in hospital, a patient wrote a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer lies hidden across 'hospITAL I Composed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping printed character, as used for emphasis, is a style of type.

clue.text: Hamper chap and I ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new arrangement, so chap and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders a picnic basket for themselves and a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' suggests a basket, but here it is the verb to impede.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede or hinder progress, as weight burdens a racehorse.

clue.text: Miser's memorial stone

explanation.surface: A tightwad's gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: First name of Dickens's skinflint Scrooge; also the stone Samuel set up as a memorial in the Bible.

clue.text: Taking food, for instance, out of a container

indicators.note: out of here means outside, so the example abbreviation goes around the container

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for instance
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Eating straight out of a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as 'from', but puts EG outside A TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming a meal is having a meal, ingesting it.
